Giants Fans Won’t Love Cam Skattebo’s Latest Actions While everyone was paying attention to the arrival of quarterback Jaxson Dart last year, the Giants also selected Skattebo in the 2025 NFL Draft with a fourth-round pick.

text:
The New York Giants are optimistic heading into the 2026 campaign, and it’s not too hard to see why. Veteran head coach John Harbaugh is taking over a team led by a dynamic young core group on both sides of the ball, and while several of these guys are recovering from injuries, there’s reason to believe this team can take a serious step forward this upcoming season.

One player who is recovering from a serious ailment is running back Cam Skattebo, as he suffered a fractured tibia, among several other injuries, shortly after earning a starting job on offense last year. Skattebo has since been working his way back to full health, but in the wake of a video popping up on social media showing him doing a backflip at Fanatics Fest on Saturday, fans have quickly taken aim at him.

Giants Fans Won’t Love Cam Skattebo’s Latest Actions

While everyone was paying attention to the arrival of quarterback Jaxson Dart last year, the Giants also selected Skattebo in the 2025 NFL Draft with a fourth-round pick. After starting the year as a backup, Skattebo quickly became the team’s starter at the running back position, as he racked up 410 yards and five touchdowns on 101 carries in eight games, while also catching 24 passes for 207 yards and two more scores.

As noted above, though, Skattebo suffered a serious leg injury against the Philadelphia Eagles that brought a premature end to his season. Considering all the promise Skattebo was showcasing, losing him certainly hurt, but beyond that, there were questions about his availability for the start of the 2026 campaign.

Skattebo has been progressing well throughout the offseason, so much so that he was confident enough to do a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the weekend. As if that wasn’t bad enough, the Giants rusher didn’t exactly stick the landing, as he fell backwards, making an already concerning incident even worse. Unsurprisingly, it didn’t take long for fans to address Skattebo’s poor decision on social media.

“I can’t even imagine John Harbaugh’s reaction to seeing this LOL,” one fan said in response to the clip.

“Any reason why Cam Skattebo appears to be trying to end his own career?” another wondered.

“It’s early, but Cam Skattebo might be the dumbest NFL player of all time,” read another post alongside this video.

Giants Hoping Cam Skattebo Will Be Ready for Week 1

Skattebo certainly is a one-of-a-kind guy, and while that makes him endearing to fans in some ways, it’s also creating problems for the Giants. Realistically, seeing Skattebo do a backflip on his recently repaired leg is the last thing the team needs, but that just doesn’t register for him. Sure, he avoided catastrophe here, but who’s to say that will be the case the next time he does something reckless?

All eyes are going to be on Skattebo once training camp gets underway later this month to see what his level of participation is as he continues to work his way back to full health. In order for New York’s offense to operate at the highest level possible, it needs Skattebo on the field, which is why he has received so much flak for this hair-brained move.

CLEVELAND, OHIO (TheOBR.com) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!

THE DAILY BLOVIATION

We're in the home stretch of the dead news period for the NFL and the Cleveland Browns, and starting to move into sites doing things like position-by-position camp previews and such. It's all the same stuff year after year, as media outlets limp through the downtime before players show up for training camp.

The rookies will show up first around mid-week, but there are no scheduled media availabilities for the team, so what you're going to get are photos of rookies walking into the Berea facility from the team's official site and not much else until the veterans show up in less than ten days.

There's no real news to talk about because, fortunately, the team has avoided any major off-field entanglements, so what a lot of sites wind up doing is writing about people writing about the Browns. I have a big white space on this Google Doc that I'm working on, so I guess I'll do the same.

I brought a couple of those types of stories with me. For instance, one is Warren Sharp putting out his 2026 front seven rankings, where he said something nice about the Browns, placing them at sixth in the league despite the loss of Myles Garrett. That's behind the Texans, Eagles, Rams, Broncos, and Seahawks, but ahead of the Steelers, the 49ers, and 27 other teams who would very much like to swap rooms with us. Top six in the league is top six in the league, regardless of who's doing the ranking in the middle of July. Someone said something nice about the Browns, so we're allowed to smile a little about it.

Meanwhile, there's endless discussion about the Browns quarterback situation, with the latest being NFL.com's Tom Pelissero noting that the quarterback horse race will be "interesting", and saying that Watson will only be tested when he steps onto the field, while being heckled by his team's own fans, and the game speeding up around him. We've seen that particular movie before, and the third or fourth sequel is rarely better than the original, which wasn't well-reviewed, either.

Meanwhile, over in the forums, the fanbase has already moved on from mourning Ethan Pocic's exit to mocking his new employer — the Watercooler thread on his signing is titled, with real affection, "Ethan Pocic Signs with Ratbirds." Ah, yes, nothing the Rats can do isn't noted with scorn. From surfing over social media, it appears there's a big gap between how Ravens fans feel about the acquisition and what the rest of the league thinks (which is not much).

Meanwhile, because the real world is boring, I at least have some interest in way-too-early 2027 mock drafts, if only to quickly scan them and see which quarterback the Browns wind up with. It's generally not Dante Moore or Arch Manning because the Browns are perceived to be just too darn good for the season to tank that badly. So, PFSN has them picking seventh and landing Edge Dylan Stewart to torment future opponents, and then drafting quarterback CJ Carr from Notre Dame with the last pick in the first round, as it's universally agreed that the Rams will win the Super Bowl these days.

So, there are a bunch of people saying things about the Browns based on what may or may not be good analysis, and my comments on them. I feel a little like an aggregator this morning, and it's icky.

I was going to go completely off-topic today and talk about how my approach to managing the OBR has changed over the years, but figured even these third-party takes are more interesting than that. Suffice it to say that the short version of that story is that the OBR has changed from an always-fun hobby to a generally fun, full-time job that sometimes requires me to make uncomfortable decisions. Maybe some other time on that one.

In the meantime, I'm planning to work on my project most of the day, then go outside, light a fire, and burn some sort of meat into oblivion. I hope you enjoy your Sunday as well, and that these bloviations have actual news to respond to in the near future.

Have a good one! GO BROWNS!

text:
During a recent appearance on Sports Radio 810, retired Pro Bowl quarterback Derek Carr shared his thoughts on Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes needing protection in the pocket from his offensive line.

"It's the hardest position in sports. It's the most valuable position in any sport, and you played it at the highest level, and then you watch him. What do you think, knowing everything that goes into playing that position? My hope for him is that they (the Chiefs) take care of him. As good as he is, we all know the talent. We know the Super Bowls," said Carr. "He and Andy (Reid) have won, and all those things, but you see what happens. It's hard to get the job done when we're scrambling or on our backs. If you give Pat (Patrick Mahomes) any time, with a run game and some play action. In every clip I've seen of the Chiefs so far, he's been under center, handing off, and I'm like, yes. I'm telling you, you give him time and protection like that, he's unbelievable."

Carr, a multiple-time Pro Bowler in his playing days, was plagued by injuries late in his career. He understands the value in solid protection from the offensive line and a consistent running game, but sees the special qualities of Mahomes.

Advertisement

"He's accurate. He throws from three-quarters. He throws from over the top sidearm. He can no-look. He can do all those things because he's learned coverage over the years. His mind is growing because he works at it, and so, as you saw at the beginning, we saw this wrong talent, right? You see these crazy plays, and you're like, "Don't do it! Oh, good throw! Oh my gosh, that was amazing! You know, all those things," said Carr. "I think what's scary for the NFL is that he's getting smarter and learning. My thing is when I watch the Chiefs, and I can say this because they can be mad at me all they want. It's like you've got to protect. If you protect, you should be in the AFC Championship fight and go to the Super Bowl every year."

Mahomes finished the 2025 season with 22 touchdown passes and 11 interceptions in 14 games before the knee injury. He also rushed for 422 yards and five touchdowns.

New York Giants fans might be flipping out over what they saw on Saturday.

Budding running back Cam Skattebo had his 2025 rookie season cut short by a devastating ankle injury. The Arizona State product was a bright spot on an otherwise dismal Giants team, with 401 rushing yards on 100 carries (4.1 yards per carry) in limited action.

While Skattebo has been transparent with his injury, recovery and rehab, the running back again showcased the health of his ankle with a backflip gone awry during Fanatics Fest this weekend.

The Giants running back took the stage a WWE event at the convention, showed off the surgically repaired ankle and proceeded to execute a nearly flawless backflip. Instead of landing securely on his feet, however, Skattebo fell, but would jump back up quickly. The East Rutherford judges might give it a 5.

On Sunday, Skattebo wanted to ease the minds of fans, making a guarantee that they will see him on the turf come the start of the season.

"I'm gonna address the elephant: I will not hurt myself before the season," he said, before continuing to explain what went wrong on the backflip.

"When I took off, I was mid-air like, 'holy cow, I'm not gonna land this, I'm way too high,'" he said. "Landed, but it had too much cushion. It wasn't a stiff, firm ground. ...

"Nothing came out from that, I'm perfectly fine. Nothing happened. We're good."

It's not the first time that Skattebo has backflipped this offseason. Another public attempt happened at teammate Brian Burns' celebrity softball game in May after hitting a home run.

The Giants are hoping he hits a lot more home runs for them, this time on the field, in 2026. With new head coach John Harbaugh's reputation of installing bruising, run-first offenses, a healthy Skattebo is expected to factor into that equation.

Cam Skattebo injury update

The Giants running back is expected to be ready for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.

Veteran Dre'Mont Jones adds a needed level of security, regardless of Landry's status, and he's a player that is in a similar mold, an every-down edge. The Patriots locked Jones up as their only multi-year signing of free agency on defense, and for good reason, they'll need to rely on the veteran who had seven sacks last season, splitting time between the Titans and Chargers.

Second-year player Elijah Ponder was the first man up this offseason with Landy out after showing solid growth as an undrafted rookie who earned a roster spot, then made growing contributions that included four sacks, two fumble recoveries and 99 snaps in the postseason. Ponder could have a breakout opportunity this season.

Jacas figures to be prominently involved in the edge rotation but was missing from minicamp practices as his injury and contract status remain uncertain. Jacas has the potential to be an all-around edge like Landry and Jones, and plays with the kind of effort and finish that made him an exciting addition to the Patriots defense. Bradyn Swinson saw some expanded opportunities this spring and has pass-rush potential, while free agent signing Jesse Luketa has 31 NFL games played with the Cardinals, including three sacks in 2024.

text:
Arsenal and England fans could have been forgiven for raising eyebrows when they saw Thomas Tuchel’s England starting XI for the World Cup third-placed play-off against France.

Declan Rice’s inclusion may have increased heart rates given the hamstring issues he has been nursing, but Bukayo Saka starting and scoring a hat-trick while completing 90 minutes just days after not being brought on in the semi-final defeat to Argentina begged the question, “Why now?” for many.

In fairness to Saka, when asked by BBC Sport if he could have played a bigger part in England’s tournament, what else would he say other than: “Of course I would have loved to have played more, but it’s too late to talk about that. I try to do my talking on the pitch.” He added “I’m fit” when pushed.

In the semi-final, Tuchel spoke of Morgan Rogers’ physicality as a reason to start, and then about the crazy nature of the second half when opting for different substitutions rather than bringing on Saka.

The German added: “Bukayo is a key player. He was ready to go in the World Cup. I still felt the responsibility as a coach and with the (injury) history he came from, to take it slow with Bukayo. He started some matches and it was a tough decision to leave him out of the semi-final.”

Saka could not train early in the World Cup because of his recent Achilles issue and Tuchel’s comments came in the context of the 24-year-old going full pelt for club and country since his teens — Saka ranked in the top two for minutes played at Arsenal for three successive seasons between the ages of 18 and 21.

The issue most may struggle to get past is not that Saka did not start against Argentina, but that he did not come on at all.

His response on the pitch in the display against France may feed result-based conclusions, but his history with England should give an indication of how critical he is to their present and future.

Saka has constantly stepped up for England at tournaments despite questions over him.

He came into Euro 2020 with some insisting he should be used as a left wing-back, but stole the show at right wing in the round-of-16 win over Germany and took a penalty in the shootout defeat to Italy in the final aged 19. At the 2022 World Cup and 2024 European Championship, the debate was over whether Phil Foden or Saka should start on the right.

Saka got the nod, and responded with important moments, including a penalty-winning foul against France in the 2022 quarter-finals, an assist for England’s only goal in their opening win over Serbia in 2024 and a late equaliser against Switzerland later in the tournament.

Before this month’s semi-final, Saka became just the third English player to assist three goals at a World Cup, averaging one every 64 minutes. These too were important, with the openers against Panama and Mexico assisted by him and scored by Jude Bellingham.

These two players are the most reliable attacking figures England will have in a post-Harry Kane world. Saka was the third top-scorer for England in this summer’s World Cup squad before the tournament began, behind Kane (aged 32) and Marcus Rashford (aged 28). Kane could play at 34 in the next Euros in 2028, but having an equally integral role at 36 at the 2030 World Cup seems unlikely.

With these tournaments in mind, the responsibility felt by Tuchel this summer and Mikel Arteta towards the back end of the season (when Saka’s minutes were managed with Arsenal) becomes even more important. Arteta cited the impact of accumulated game time across seasons, specifically in relation to Saka, days after he tore a hamstring in December 2024, and did look to rotate more on the right wing with the signing of Noni Madueke last season.

Neither Arteta nor Tuchel will want to be in situations where they cannot use one of the most influential players in their biggest games, so continuing to protect him could be vital in upcoming seasons and tournaments.

Comparisons were made between how Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain use players before this year’s Champions League final, with nine Arsenal players playing more than 2,000 league minutes compared with PSG’s three.

While the strength of the Premier League compared with Ligue 1 makes rotation more difficult, the demands on Saka have been non-stop since he arrived in the first team.

Saka will get at least three weeks off now, but the demands of a new season should not override a clear need to be eased back in, even if the winger says he is fit.

He featured in both of Arsenal’s opening league matches after helping England reach the final of the last two European Championships. The weight of three points in the Premier League contributed to that, but looking ahead to the 2026-27 season and beyond, more long-term thinking would benefit the futures of Saka, Arsenal and England.

He will deliver when called upon — it is just a matter of enabling him to answer the call in the best way possible.

text:
Golf

Scottie Scheffler breaks silence on Bryson DeChambeau rules violation at The Open

Scottie Scheffler refused to comment on the Bryson DeChambeau fiasco at The Open Championship on Saturday. However, now that the Open Championship has finished, Scheffler clearly felt like it was the right time to share his opinion. DeChambeau was just one stroke adrift of the lead after he holed out for a birdie on the final hole on Friday. However, that quickly turned into a three-shot deficit after Bryson DeChambeau was informed of a potential rules violation earlier in his round at The Open on the fifth hole. DeChambeau was penalized two strokes after his second round at The Open finished and he actually threatened not to turn up and play on Sunday. Rory McIlroy ripped into DeChambeau after his round on Saturday, suggesting that it was a clear and obvious breach of the rules from the American. And now world number one Scottie Scheffler has offered his take on the whole situation. Scottie Scheffler comments on Bryson DeChambeau rules violation at The Open Scheffler responded when asked whether he is now comfortable talking about the DeChambeau incident on Friday at Birkdale. “No. I’ve been really focused on the tournament,“ he said. “I think that opens up a greater discussion that — all I can really say is I think maybe we need to be a little bit more strict in the way that we are policing guys, but it’s a little bit of a balance because you’ve got certain guys like a Bryson who every shot he hits is going to be shown on TV. “When you have camera angles that are far away, things can look different than they do when you’re right there. “We’ve done a good job of — I don’t know, I hate saying stuff out here because I don’t want anything to get taken out of context. All I’ll say is Bryson, I’ve known him for a long time, and he’s a lot of things, but he’s definitely not a cheater. “I’ve never seen him cheat once, whether we were having a putting contest on the putting green or chipping contest, or anytime we played amateur golf, I never saw anything suspicious. “When you’re watching him there from that camera angle, maybe he was a touch careless around his ball, but I don’t think he did anything intentionally. “We’ve seen penalties happen with — like you remember Jon Rahm a couple years ago at the Memorial when his ball moved in the rough, and it’s like to the naked eye, can you really tell that? “I think sometimes it’s just a difficult position in the game of golf. When I was growing up, if this was the line between things that were — like if this was the line, here are the rules and this was the right side of it and this is when you’re doing things against the rule, you always tried to stray really far that way. I feel like at times, sometimes you see players maybe push it a little bit further than they should.“ Bryson DeChambeau is not a cheater, says Scottie Scheffler Scheffler insisted that he has known DeChambeau for a long time now and that the LIV Golf star is certainly ‘not a cheater’. “I think we need to kind of get back to the traditions of the game and maybe we do need to police things a little bit more strictly in the game,“ the world number one said. “But like I said, it’s a tough line to kind of cross. So that’s why it’s hard for me to say anything like this. Bryson is a guy that I’ve known for a really long time. Like I said, he’s not a cheater.“ Bryson DeChambeau will be delighted to hear those comments from Scottie Scheffler after his troubles at The Open. The LIV Golf star has received much criticism this week but at least he has Scheffler in his corner.

NFL

Ian Rapoport gives grim update on Baker Mayfield's contract talks

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are less than two weeks away from the start of training camp. That means the clock is ticking, and Baker Mayfield still hasn't gotten the deal he's looking for. The former No. 1 pick let it be known that he wouldn't negotiate a new deal after the start of training camp, meaning he's getting dangerously close to playing on the final year of his contract before hitting free agency in 2027. According to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, both sides have been in constant talks recently, but the situation still hasn't changed. Baker Mayfield may not get a new deal before training camp “They have had conversations; they have had extensive talks. Does not feel to me like they’re close, and this deadline is coming,” Rapoport said on “The Insiders.” Mayfield is reportedly looking to get top dollar and make at least $55 million a year. He has led the Buccaneers to the playoffs in 2023 and 2024, and he threw for 3,693 yards, 26 touchdowns and 11 picks last season. Injuries derailed the team's aspirations, but he played well enough when they were at full strength. Consistency has never been Mayfield's strength, and that, plus his reluctance to avoid hits, might raise concerns in Florida about a potential long-term pact. Even so, he's held his end of the bargain after signing a three-year, $100 million contract that may have saved his spiraling career, and he's by far the Buccaneers' best option right now. The clock is ticking, and these sides aren't seeing eye to eye. And as much as they could always get a deal done during the season, it looks like they could be heading toward divorce.

MLB

Shohei Ohtani announcement could pivot Dodgers at MLB trade deadline

The Los Angeles Dodgers may be looking to add to the rotation at the upcoming MLB trade deadline as questions about the health of Shohei Ohtani's knee linger. On Sunday morning, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts revealed that Ohtani will not make his scheduled start in Philadelphia against the Phillies on Wednesday as he continues to battle lingering inflammation in his left knee. Ohtani has not pitched since July 3 after it was revealed he had been dealing with the inflammation and irritation since a June 11 start in Pittsburgh. "We just want to continue to give (the knee) the best chance to get into a good spot," Roberts told reporters, via Katie Woo of The Athletic. "It's going to be some time and I'd say that it's not going to be a day-to-day thing," Roberts added, via Sonja Chen of MLB.com. Those words are a bit ominous for a Dodgers rotation that is also missing Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell from its core. Snell had loose bodies removed from his left elbow but could return in early August if all goes well. Glasnow, meanwhile, has been sidelined with back spasms since early May and is reportedly only throwing fastballs while trying to work his way back. Will Shohei Ohtani's health determine the Dodgers' trade deadline moves? If those two do return in August, it would certainly be a boost for the Los Angeles rotation for the season's stretch run. However, with Ohtani's situation keeping him off the mound, could this mean the Dodgers may go big at the trade deadline for another front-line starter? A splash move for Detroit's Tarik Skubal or another well-known name may make more sense after hearing Ohtani will not be pitching for "some time." Keep in mind that Ohtani has already pitched 85.2 innings this season after throwing just 47.0 innings last year after recovering from elbow surgery. Keeping Ohtani healthy and ready for the postseason would seem to be a priority for Roberts and the Dodgers, especially with his increased workload already this season. Of course, the Dodgers have to get to October and have work to do to ensure they will have home-field advantage throughout the National League postseason. Los Angeles entered Sunday's action just one game ahead of the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the NL. While Ohtani can still do damage for the Dodgers at the plate serving as the team's designated hitter, keeping him off the mound may be a sign that the Dodgers will once again be one of the biggest trade deadline buyers.

title: NFL Trade Rumors Top 100 Players: 60-51 - NFLTradeRumors.co
description:
July is top 100 season in the NFL as everyone tries to kill the days until training camp and the start of the new season.
The time has come for the 2026 version of our NFL Trade Rumors Top 100 Players.
56 – 49ers QB Brock Purdy Purdy might be the most polarizing player on this list, with legions on either side who will insist this is either far too high a ranking or far too low.
55 – Chargers LT Rashawn Slater Slater missed the entire 2025 season due to a torn patellar tendon on August 7 last year, one of several major injuries the Chargers absorbed.
He was eighth in the NFL in pass block win rate at 94 percent according to ESPN.
text:
July is top 100 season in the NFL as everyone tries to kill the days until training camp and the start of the new season. Unfortunately, the official top 100 list from the league is not good. We’re not trying to hate; it’s just a well-accepted fact at this point in time.

For five years, we’ve been trying to do better. The time has come for the 2026 version of our NFL Trade Rumors Top 100 Players. Instead of using player polls, we aim to better reflect reality with traditional and advanced statistical analysis, evaluations from league personnel, positional value, awards, career trajectory and, of course, the good old-fashioned gut check. Our hope is to give more credit to players who are overlooked, either because they don’t play a glamorous position or because they’re not household names (yet).

We’ll have updates daily over the next couple of weeks, so keep checking back!

Previous Entries:

NFLTR Top 100: 100-91

NFLTR Top 100: 90-81

NFLTR Top 100: 80-71

NFLTR Top 100: 70-61

Resources:

Pro Football Reference

QB advanced stats

Win rates from ESPN for OL and DL

PFF advanced stats (grades, pass rush productivity, blocking efficiency, coverage stats)

ESPN WR tracking metrics

Past NFLTR Top 100s

60 – 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey

No player carried a heavier load than McCaffrey last season. His 413 touches not only led the league, they were the most of any player since 2014. Excluding quarterbacks, there wasn’t another player who was relied upon more by his team to generate offense — especially because of all the injuries the 49ers navigated in 2025, including to the quarterback position. McCaffrey rushed for 1,202 yards and 10 scores while adding another 102 receptions for 924 yards and seven touchdowns. He was within shouting distance of being the first-ever player to record multiple 1,000-1,000 seasons (rushing and receiving yards).

Given McCaffrey’s injury history, it’s an open question whether the 49ers can keep putting that much on his plate. His efficiency suffered in 2025, perhaps because it was predictable how often the 49ers were going to lean on him. He averaged less than four yards per carry and PFF charted him with the lowest percentage of yards on breakaway runs since an injury-maligned 2020 season. Still, he forced 74 total missed tackles in 2025, so the idea that McCaffrey was just a volume hog doesn’t stand up to scrutiny.

59 – Patriots WR A.J. Brown

Brown suffered through one of the worst statistical seasons of his career this past season and he didn’t suffer in silence, which is probably why he’s currently in New England instead of Philadelphia. He just turned 29 last month, so it’s natural for questions about a potential decline to come up, especially since Brown has been managing a knee injury for a while now.

Yet some context is needed. Even in a “down” season, Brown topped 1,000 yards receiving on a run-first offense and scored seven touchdowns. In ESPN’s open score and PFF’s receiving grade — both metrics that seek to evaluate a wide receiver’s performance even if he’s not targeted on a passing play — Brown ranked No. 9 and No. 13 out of over a hundred wideouts. He had an excellent 2.88 yards per route run against man coverage, No. 8 in the NFL.

The proverbial “lost step” can be hard to spot in the NFL, and there are mixed opinions from film watchers whether Brown slowed down in 2025. His production was down but that’s so heavily impacted by the offensive environment, and let’s just say the Eagles had their challenges last year. The rest of the analytics suggest Brown remains a top-ten receiver, and he has a fresh start with a star quarterback to try and prove that this year.

58 – Falcons WR Drake London

London was on a tear before a PCL injury blunted his momentum and his statistical finish to the season. He topped 100 yards receiving in five out of nine games to start the season before the injury, then had 109 yards and a touchdown combined over the final three after he returned. He finished with 68 catches, 919 yards and seven touchdowns in 12 games after a breakout 1,200-yard season the year prior.

Perhaps the injury explains some interesting splits in the advanced stats. London is a big wideout at 6-4 and 215 pounds who moonlighted on the basketball team in college at USC, so he wins more with physicality and positioning than by pure speed. Still, an open score of 47 is below average and drastically worse than his career-high 84 mark the season before. London’s numbers against man coverage were also uninspiring, but he had a superb 89.9 receiving grade from PFF. Look for a bounceback for Atlanta’s No. 1 receiver this year if he can maintain good health.

57 – Lions QB Jared Goff

The book on Goff has been out for a while. He’s a pocket-only passer, so creating pressure is a recipe for getting him to miss throws and make mistakes. However, that’s easier said than done with Detroit’s offensive line and scheme. And Goff has reached a point where he’s the puncher far more often than the punching bag. Last season was his third straight year of over 30 passing touchdowns, 4,500 yards and at least a 67 percent completion rate. He protected the ball well, too, despite slightly worse protection than prior years. His turnover-worthy play rate of two percent was fourth-best, and PFF charted him with an adjusted completion percentage (accounting for drops and removing throwaways) of over 80 percent, tops among all passers.

56 – 49ers QB Brock Purdy

Purdy might be the most polarizing player on this list, with legions on either side who will insist this is either far too high a ranking or far too low. Not to take the easy way out, but it feels like reality is somewhere in the middle. There’s no question Purdy benefits from a top-notch supporting offensive infrastructure, from play-caller and architect Kyle Shanahan to quality skill players and protection.

However, Purdy plays his part in the system exceptionally well. He has just enough quick-twitch athleticism to create on his own from time to time when a teammate busts an assignment or Shanahan hasn’t dialed up the perfect play call. His pressure-to-sack rate of 3.73 percent was the third-lowest of all quarterbacks last season, per PFF. Limited to nine games because of a turf toe injury that he pushed through (another credit to Purdy), the former Mr. Irrelevant still blistered the stat sheet in the games he played. He put up 23 total touchdowns in a little over half a season of work. He led the NFL in success rate, ranked second in completion percentage over expected and finished ninth in adjusted net yards per attempt.

Plenty of people would have loved to generate a quarterback controversy between Purdy and his injury replacement, former Shanahan draft crush Mac Jones, who kept San Francisco’s season on the rails in seven starts. Shanahan has had success with a lot of different quarterbacks, leading to the idea that Purdy might just be a replaceable cog in the system. Jones did play pretty well — Purdy was just authoritatively better, nipping that narrative in the bud.

55 – Chargers LT Rashawn Slater

Slater missed the entire 2025 season due to a torn patellar tendon on August 7 last year, one of several major injuries the Chargers absorbed. Athletes say a torn patellar tendon is even more grueling to rehab than a torn ACL, but Slater has had plenty of time and it should be reasonable to project him to pick up roughly where he left off. We ranked him No. 45 last season:

“Slater returned to the Pro Bowl for the second time in his four years following a slight rough patch the past two years after an outstanding rookie debut. The 26-year-old reasserted himself as one of the top young tackles in football and his all-around game is an excellent fit for the Chargers’ run-heavy offense. Slater finished 10th among all tackles in ESPN’s run block win rate with a mark of 79 percent, and he had PFF’s seventh-highest run blocking grade. He was great as a pass protector too, allowing just 26 total pressures on the year and three sacks.”

54 – Ravens OLB Trey Hendrickson

Hendrickson played in just seven games in his final season with the Bengals. He tried to push through a sports hernia injury and reinjured it, sidelining him through the rest of the season. He was clearly diminished after the injury, too, so there was a sense in Cincinnati that he wasn’t exactly rushing to get back on the field at less than full strength in a contract year. That’s the downside for teams when a negotiation goes as sour as it did between the two sides last year.

At 31 years old, Hendrickson now goes to Baltimore, where the big question is what the Ravens will be getting. His 2025 cameo still featured four sacks and a forced fumble, while PFF charted him with a 21.5 percent win rate that would keep him in the company he’s accustomed to at the top of the edge rusher hierarchy. So it seems the odds are good that the Ravens are getting a top-notch pass rusher. Hendrickson’s play against the run has continued to wane, though, and while the Ravens aren’t risking as much as they would have in the Maxx Crosby trade, the Hendrickson signing is still a gamble.

53 – Steelers OLB T.J. Watt

Watt was mostly healthy this past season outside of a freak accident when his lung was collapsed in a dry needling session. That caused him to miss three games and threw off his conditioning when he returned. But even before the injury, Watt wasn’t his usual prolific self in 2025. He finished with just seven sacks on the season, his first time in double digits in a relatively healthy year since he was a rookie.

A deeper dive doesn’t reduce the concern. Watt didn’t place on ESPN’s pass rush win rate leaderboard for the first time in a while. PFF charted him with 49 total pressures, 32nd out of 130 qualifying edge rushers and one of his least disruptive outputs since he was a rookie. He ranked 82nd in PFF’s pass rush productivity score. He did still do usual Watt things by stuffing the rest of the stat sheet with big plays, forcing three fumbles, picking off two passes and breaking up eight in total. Still, there’s a reason there’s some concern in Pittsburgh about Watt and why he’s slipped so far on this list.

52 – Giants LT Andrew Thomas

It wasn’t a completely healthy season for Thomas, who missed four games after losing 18 games to injury over the previous two seasons. But he was on the field enough for the Giants in 2025 to remind the league that he’s one of the top tackles in football when healthy. He was eighth in the NFL in pass block win rate at 94 percent according to ESPN. PFF charted him with just 13 total pressures given up all year and one sack. In true pass sets, which are usually known passing situations when the defense can dial up a blitz or pin its ears back and rush, Thomas turned in an absolutely stellar 98.1 percent efficiency rate — No. 2 among all tackles. Throw in a quality 84.6 run blocking grade from PFF and it was a strong campaign.

51 – Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs

Running backs have fought back against the perception that they’re interchangeable and disposable, and slowly the tide is starting to shift. Much of that is due to exciting new players like Gibbs, who made his third straight Pro Bowl in 2025 and asserted his grip on the Detroit backfield. He flirted with 2,000 yards from scrimmage for the second straight season and scored 18 total touchdowns.

Gibbs is both a talented runner and receiver, and thanks to his game-breaking speed he is a legitimate threat to score a touchdown every time he touches the football. PFF credited him with 87 forced missed tackles between rushes and receptions, and 40.6 percent of his rushing yardage came on his 14 runs of 15 yards or longer. That speed and skill would make it difficult for the Lions to replace him with just anyone, and it’s why Gibbs is likely set to sign a deal that will move the running back market forward at some point this summer.

Simon is a chess addict who regularly plays against his Spain team-mates, including Dani Olmo. Simon told Spanish channel RTVE he was “100 per cent” the best chess player in the squad — which is disputed by Olmo.

David Raya

Raya may now be a Premier League champion with Arsenal but at 19 he was playing for Southport in the fifth tier of English football. His career took off after an FA Cup third-round tie against Championship side Derby County in January 2015.

Joan Garcia

Garcia is from Sallent, a Catalan village of 7,000 inhabitants and loves the mountains, where he spends much of his free time. He is known for having a cool head and always plays the same two songs when getting off the team bus — Not Afraid by Eminem and Live Your Life by T.I.

Defenders

Pedro Porro

Porro is really close to his grandfather. The Spanish FA posted an emotional video showing a video call between the pair after Porro’s first international goal against Austria earlier in the tournament. His grandfather joked he had pushed the ball into the net for the defender.

Marcos Llorente

Llorente has become known for his unusual and often controversial lifestyle, including spending as much time as possible in the sun without suncream, as he doesn’t believe in its benefits. He wears yellow-tinted glasses during the day and red-tinted glasses at night.

Aymeric Laporte

Laporte was born in the French town of Agen and won the Under-19 European Championship with France in 2011 and 2012, before switching allegiances to Spain after moving to Bilbao’s Athletic Club as a youngster.

Pau Cubarsi

Cubarsi is from a family of carpenters and made a stool for a final-year project in sixth form. “If one day football doesn’t go so well, carpentry will always be there, that’s clear,” he told El Mundo last year.

Marc Pubill

Pubill is extremely superstitious. His mother Ana told Spanish radio station Cadena Cope this week about the defender’s curious pre-match routine: “He steps onto the pitch with his right foot, he jumps up three times and he touches his bottom”.

Eric Garcia

A football geek who watches at least four matches a day on weekends — mostly La Liga and the Premier League — on multiple screens. He is also a huge NBA fan and watches as many games as he can.

Marc Cucurella

Cucurella and coach Luis de la Fuente are very close. In an interview with Cope, the left-back promised to tattoo De la Fuente’s face on his body if Spain win the World Cup. He didn’t say where.

Midfielders

Rodri

Rodri is the only player in the squad without a public Instagram, X or TikTok account and didn’t even post a picture of himself with the Ballon d’Or he won in 2024. “I don’t care about social media or £400 trainers,” he wrote in an article for The Players’ Tribune.

Martin Zubimendi

Another keen chess player in the squad who was champion of the Basque province of Gipuzkoa in that discipline as a child. He was in contention to become chess champion of the Basque Country, but didn’t go to the tournament as it clashed with a football competition.

Pedri

Pedri possesses a lovely head of hair but strangely the 23-year-old quite fancies throwing it all away. “I’ve always wanted to go bald, I don’t know why,” he wrote in a Q and A session with fans on YouTube channel The Residency in 2024. Perhaps it is something to do with his childhood idol being Andres Iniesta.

Fabian Ruiz

Ruiz comes from the same Andalusian town as Gavi near Seville, Los Palacios y Villafranca. Every time he has won a major trophy, his hometown has marked the occasion by giving him his weight in tomatoes — around 80 kilograms’ worth.

Mikel Merino

Merino celebrates all his goals for Spain by running around the corner flag. That was his father Miguel Merino’s goal celebration — in tribute to his mother (Mikel’s grandmother) — after he scored for Osasuna against Stuttgart in 1991. At that stadium 35 years later, Mikel scored a winning header for Spain against Germany at the Euros.

Gavi

Gavi is a big music lover who took solace in his favourite artists’ work after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in 2023. He likes everything from Pearl Jam to Michael Jackson and Blur to Taylor Swift and One Direction — even striking up a good relationship with Louis Tomlinson.

Alex Baena

Baena was punched by Real Madrid’s Federico Valverde after a La Liga match at the Bernabeu in 2023. He told Cope during this tournament he “almost left football” because of that incident and how it affected his family — before he effectively eliminated Valverde’s Uruguay in the group stage with his winning goal in Guadalajara.

Forwards

Mikel Oyarzabal

In his early 20s, Oyarzabal combined playing for Real Sociedad with studying for a university degree in business administration and management, living in a city-centre student flat with two school friends.

Lamine Yamal

Nothing can beat those photos of Lionel Messi bathing a baby Yamal, but did you know he started studying cookery after getting the equivalent of his high-school diploma at the Euros? That’s what he told late-night show El Hormiguero in 2024, although he admitted at the time the best he could produce was chicken and chips…

Ferran Torres

He was born on February 29, 2000 — a leap year — so his actual birthday only happens every four years. His self-given nickname is ‘the shark’, which he chose in summer 2023 after consulting with a sports psychologist, hoping to project a more fearsome image.

Borja Iglesias

After former Spanish FA president Luis Rubiales kissed Jenni Hermoso without consent following the 2023 Women’s World Cup final, Iglesias said he would not play for the men’s national team again while Rubiales remained. Javier Bardem has worn an ‘Iglesias 26’ Spain shirt in the stands at this World Cup in recognition of the striker’s stance on social issues. Iglesias and Hermoso — who is working as a pundit at this tournament — shared an emotional embrace after last week’s semi-final.

Dani Olmo

Olmo speaks fluent Croatian after leaving Barcelona’s academy aged 16 to join Dinamo Zagreb. He even gave press conferences in Croatian there and also speaks Catalan, Spanish, English and a little German from his time at RB Leipzig.

Victor Munoz

Munoz is a very rare case of a player who developed at both Barcelona’s academy from 2014-2017 and Real Madrid’s youth system from 2021-2025. But he only truly broke out last season after leaving Madrid for Osasuna, before securing a big move to Liverpool this summer.

Nico Williams

Wiliams’ parents Maria and Felix were born in Ghana and travelled across the Sahara Desert to the Spanish enclave of Melilla, in North Africa, when Maria was pregnant with Nico’s older brother, Inaki. They both play for Athletic Club, but Inaki represents Ghana at international level.

Yeremy Pino

Pino was all set to play for Spain at the 2019 Under-17 World Cup before he was hit in the face in training a few days before by an accidentally misplaced pass from Pedri. That caused an eye injury, which ruled him out of that tournament.

Argentina

Goalkeepers

Emiliano Martinez

Martinez is nicknamed “Dibu” because of a striking resemblance when he was younger to the main character from the hit 1990s Argentinian TV series Mi familia es un dibujo (‘My family is a drawing’), who has reddish hair and a face full of freckles.

Geronimo Rulli

Rulli’s role model is Benji Price, the goalkeeper from the anime series Captain Tsubasa. He was once gifted a print of the character by the show’s creator Yoichi Takahashi and said he would display it at his home as if it were “more than a trophy”.

Juan Musso

Musso is a firm believer in the power of yoga. In 2021, he told Argentinian outlet Infobae he had been practising it for six years. “It changed my way of thinking,” he said.

Defenders

Gonzalo Montiel

His younger brother Santiago is also a footballer and in 2025 won the Puskas Award for scoring the best goal in the world — an overhead kick from distance for Independiente against Independiente Rivadavia in the Argentinian top flight in May.

Nahuel Molina

Molina spent time at an Argentinian offshoot of Barcelona’s academy from 2011-12, which included a trip to Spain to train at La Masia. “I’d never got on a plane before,” he told La Nacion in 2021. “In the first few days, I didn’t touch the ball; their quality was different.”

Lisandro Martinez

Like many Argentinians, Martinez is not afraid to express his emotions — but the man known as “the butcher” for his style of play has said his partner Muriel showed him “a lot about being a man”. “I love to cry, I love to express myself, I love to give love,” he told Filo News this year.

Nicolas Otamendi

Otamendi’s path to professional football was unconventional. As a youngster, boxing was his main sport at first. He is nicknamed “The General,” a reference to his signature military-style goal celebration.

Leonardo Balerdi

In 2023, a Marseille supporter claimed to be staging a hunger strike outside the club’s training ground until Balerdi was offloaded after a series of mistakes in games. The defender seemed to see the positive side in a 2024 interview with L’Equipe. “I like when people speak badly about me; it motivates me too,” he said.

Cristian Romero

He is known as “Cuti” Romero. The nickname was given to him as a child by his elder sister Aldana, because she couldn’t say “Cristian” — just one fun footnote in The Athletic’s in-depth report from 2021.

Facundo Medina

He grew up in Villa Fiorito, a neighbourhood in Lomas de Zamora, within the Buenos Aires province. The most famous person to come from that neighbourhood? Argentina legend Diego Maradona.

Nicolas Tagliafico

As well as football, Tagliafico is a talented artist who draws anime cartoons. A video on his YouTube channel from 2024 showed him drawing some of the main characters from the Dragon Ball series.

Midfielders

Leandro Paredes

The Boca Juniors midfielder was scouted by their fierce Buenos Aires rivals River Plate when he was five years old but locked himself in his room and cried when River officials came to his house, as he told streaming channel Olga in 2024. Six months later, Boca came calling.

Rodrigo De Paul

Argentina have a ritual involving candy before each match thanks to De Paul’s late grandfather Osvaldo — so much so that the Argentinian FA confirmed to The Athletic they travelled to the U.S. with 500 kilograms of the stuff.

De Paul and his team-mates chew on candy before each match for good luck and as a tribute to Osvaldo, who would take his grandson to training when he was younger and give him a few coins to buy himself a treat each time.

Exequiel Palacios

Palacios might have joined Real Madrid when he was at River Plate, telling Spanish newspaper Marca that club staff “travelled to put me through a medical, but ultimately it didn’t work out because of something to do with injuries”. He still got to train under Madrid icon and future Blancos coach Xabi Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen.

Enzo Fernandez

Enzo is named after the River Plate legend Enzo Francescoli, who represented Uruguay at two World Cups. Fernandez started his professional career at River Plate in Argentina before moving to Benfica (and then Chelsea).

Alexis Mac Allister

His older brother, also a footballer (who plays for Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise), was named Kevin Mac Allister after the character in Home Alone. He didn’t realise this until a journalist asked him about it when he was 18.

Giovani Lo Celso

Lo Celso missed the 2022 World Cup through injury but it did mean he was present for the birth of his daughter. His wife’s waters broke when Lionel Messi scored against Mexico, a goal that rescued Argentina from the brink of elimination.

Speaking to TyC Sports in 2023, he said: “It was in the middle of the match, Leo scored the goal and we had to leave. I remember that I was watching the game on the phone on the way to the hospital. I watched Enzo’s (Fernandez) goal from the car. Later, we went in there and at dawn my daughter was born. I was present all the time; it is something unique, something magical, that life allowed me to witness.”

Valentin Barco

As a youngster at Boca Juniors, Barco travelled for four hours to and from training sessions with his mother and father from 25 de Mayo, a city in Buenos Aires province.

Forwards

Lionel Messi

His first contract with Barcelona was written on a napkin, which was later auctioned for nearly $1million in 2024. Perhaps more curiously, Messi’s mother named him after Lionel Richie — and the pair met last year.

Nico Paz

Nico is the son of another Argentina international, Pablo Paz, who represented them at the 1998 World Cup in France. Nico was born in Tenerife but chose to play for Argentina over Spain.

Thiago Almada

Almada is one of many Argentinian players who have escaped poverty through football. He is from the same Buenos Aires neighbourhood, Fuerte Apache, as former Manchester City, Manchester United and national team forward Carlos Tevez.

Nicolas Gonzalez

Gonzalez has played everywhere across the frontline and at left-back for his country — the position from which he made his breakthrough in a November 2020 World Cup qualifier against Paraguay, scoring a header. “People from outside asked: ‘Who is Nico Gonzalez, where does he play?’,” he said in a radio interview with Oral Deportiva. “I really liked shutting people up.”

Giuliano Simeone

Giuliano, who is the son of his Atletico Madrid coach Diego Simeone, suffered a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle during Alaves’ 2023 pre-season. Diego was flying to Madrid at the time and only found out upon landing, driving to the Basque Country to be with his son. Giuliano hadn’t even played in the Spanish top flight yet, but told his agents he would play at the 2026 World Cup.

Lautaro Martinez

Nicknamed ‘El Toro’ (the bull) for his aggressive style of play, Lautaro is also deeply religious. He tucks an image of Our Lady of Lujan, the patroness of Argentina, inside one of his shin guards when playing.

Jose Manuel Lopez

Known as “El Flaco” (the skinny one), he arrived at Brazilian club Palmeiras looking very… well, skinny. He managed to gain 10 kilograms of muscle mass through a personalised nutrition and fitness training programme.

Julian Alvarez

He was given the moniker “La Araña” (the spider) during his childhood because of how quickly he glided across the pitch — as if he had eight legs. The nickname stuck and has carried on into his professional career, with Alvarez even celebrating goals as if he were Spider-Man.

title: NFL players love wearing their 'slippers and slides, baby!' - ESPN
authors: Michael DiRocco, Ben Strauss, Rich Cimini, Mike Reiss, Ryan McFadden, Courtney Cronin, DJ Bien-Aime, Jeremy Fowler, Bill Barnwell, Tristan H. Cockcroft
description:
NFL players' feet take a beating.
Either way, the definitions, and use-cases for both slides and slippers overlap and are utilized in different ways from the NFL players who shared their footwear habits with ESPN.
IF AN NFL player isn't wearing slippers around the facility, he's almost certainly wearing slides.
Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. started wearing Oofos recovery slippers last season as well as soft slides in the offseason.
WHETHER IT'S SLIPPERS, regular slides and sandals, or specific recovery footwear, NFL players are serious about taking care of their feet.
text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Do the shoes really make the man?

Not for New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins, who likes to go barefoot as often as possible -- including at practice -- because he said he believes it helps strengthen his lower body, improve foot dexterity, and it improves his connection to the ground.

For everybody else in the NFL, however, their choice of footwear is important, particularly when they're in meetings, the cafeteria and the locker room. So some players opt for a more informal type of footwear.

"Slippers and slides, baby!" Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon said. "It really started in college, where we were taught about how everything about your body matters, from your feet to your shins to your hamstrings. Everything plays a part."

NFL players' feet take a beating. They get stepped on, kicked, battered, stuffed into tight cleats. It's even worse for players who regularly practice or play on artificial turf, which isn't as forgiving as natural grass. That makes taking care of -- and pampering -- their feet a priority.

"I feel like that's always been important," Seahawks linebacker Derick Hall said. "A lot of guys will walk across the field barefoot just trying to stay grounded. They say it helps stimulate healing and the recovery process, so we harp on that a lot. Our medical staff and strength staff stay on that a lot.

"I don't have an absurd amount, but I have about three or four pairs of slides and slippers at my disposal at the facility at all times."

Players across the league use both throughout the season for comfort and recovery. But if you're expecting something normal, well, you've clearly never been inside an NFL locker room.

Players can be eclectic, creative and maybe even a little whimsical about their footwear.

THERE ARE TWO kinds of slipper wearers in the NFL. Those who wear normal slippers and those who ... don't.

Washington Commanders defensive end Javontae Jean-Baptiste is definitely among the latter, because his latest choice was a pair of purple bear claw mules, which he purchased last season for $115 from Bravest Studios.

They're not his only pair.

"My first pair was brown, like a grizzly bear," explains Jean-Baptiste, who said he ordered a pair of blue bear claw mules last season for teammate Dante Fowler Jr. "Then I saw the purple, and it's my favorite color, so I got that. ... They're comfortable."

Slides are typically open-toed and backless and are usually designed for more outdoor use, while slippers often are indoor comfort wear. Either way, the definitions, and use-cases for both slides and slippers overlap and are utilized in different ways from the NFL players who shared their footwear habits with ESPN.

San Francisco 49ers linebacker Nick Martin estimates he has 10 pairs of varied varieties of slippers, including wolves, dogs and sharks (which he wore on his first day of rookie minicamp in 2025).

"I'm pretty comfortable with who I am," said Martin, who was spotted wearing dog slippers on the field before a preseason game. "And I've always worn 'em, so why change?"

Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. also has a pair of brown bear claw slippers, which, as we've seen, clearly isn't unusual. But he also has a pair of Incredible Hulk slippers, which he saw while scrolling on Instagram and purchased right after training camp.

"I used to like the Incredible Hulk growing up a little bit, so seeing those, I was like, 'I've got to get those,'" Thomas said. "So Spider-Man and Incredible Hulk were my two favorite characters growing up. They didn't have anything for Spider-Man."

Thomas said he wore his slippers regularly early in the season but cut down in favor of sneakers and slides with more structure and support as the season wore on. He even wore the bear claw slippers to an indoor walk-through the day before a game. He regretted that pretty quickly.

"[Coach] Liam [Coen] came in and he was like, 'Bro,'" Thomas said. "He was just laughing at me. He had everybody laughing, dying at me."

Minnesota Vikings cornerback Isaiah Rodgers doesn't exactly wear slippers, but he does have a cover for his cleats that look like slippers. Not an animal, though: Hot Wheels.

And then there's Carolina Panthers linebacker Nic Scourton, who wears normal slippers.

Kind of.

The day after the Panthers beat the Atlanta Falcons 30-0 in their 2025 home opener, Scourton was sporting a pair of fuzzy orange Mari slippers, which he said he purchased while in college, that were allegedly priced at $900.

IF AN NFL player isn't wearing slippers around the facility, he's almost certainly wearing slides. And just like slippers, there's a huge variety.

Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. started wearing Oofos recovery slippers last season as well as soft slides in the offseason. Using the recovery slippers was his mother's idea, but Pitts was resistant at first.

"My mom actually mentioned them to me, and I was like, 'No, no, no,'" Pitts said. "And then one day I was on the web and looked them up. I might have been in the mall, actually. They have a store. And I was like, 'Let me get a pair of these.' And then I tried them, and I ordered a couple of pairs."

Turns out his mom did know best, because Pitts loved them.

"It's a recovery shoe," he said. "You're on your feet damn near all day, so that's a good thing to have. ... I just love to take care of my feet. Those are my wheels."

Pitts caught a career-high 88 passes for 928 yards and five touchdowns last season and joked that those slippers might have helped.

"They've definitely played a part," he said with a laugh. "They take care of my feet, for sure."

Foot care is something NFL trainers and teams take seriously.

"The body is really a kinematic chain, right? Everything in your body, it's all connected obviously, but everything starts with your feet," said Jeff Ferguson, the Jaguars' vice president of player health and performance. "So, whether that's your plantar fascia or your arch or whether that's your ankle joint, all your motion -- even your big toe motion -- directly impacts knee movement, hip movement, all sorts of things.

"So, we spend an inordinate amount of time making sure that with our equipment guys that proper footwear is in place from a recovery standpoint, preventative aspects. Some guys need corrective insoles, some guys don't. We really want to work range of motion, so the more motion and flexibility you have, that's really important as you go up the [kinematic] chain, particularly to prevent soft tissue injuries."

Falcons safety Jessie Bates III prefers Nike ReactX Rejuvena8 slides. They fit his more casual vibe, he said, plus he feels his feet get compressed while wearing cleats and the slides allow his feet to rest and stretch out.

"Some people come to work dressed. Some people wear shoes," he said. "I'm the type of guy, I throw on a sweatsuit and I slide on some slides and call it a day. But I got every color in the Nike ReactX and I just slip those on every day."

Seahawks tight end AJ Barner wears slippers at home, which help his feet recover, but he's a proponent of using YogaToes, which are toe separators made from medical-grade gel.

"If you want to take care of your feet, put the YogaToes on," he said. "They like space your toes out. After you've had your feet in cleats all day, it really relaxes your feet. I keep them at the house for sure."

WHETHER IT'S SLIPPERS, regular slides and sandals, or specific recovery footwear, NFL players are serious about taking care of their feet. It's the one part of their body that's used on every single play and an injury can derail a season.

"It is very important for players to take care of their feet. Players need to be comfortable and not think about their feet when they are playing," Falcons head of equipment operations Joey Galioto said. "Foot care and maintenance can be very impactful in a positive or negative way on a player's performance.

"We definitely make it a huge point of emphasis with all of our players no matter the time of year -- training, running, lifting, playing football -- grass, turf, bad weather, bad field conditions ... it all matters."

Whether focused on good foot health or having fun, off-field footwear is a part of NFL player culture.

"It [taking care of their feet] is massive," Patriots linebacker Chad Muma said. "With how active we are all day, being able to get on some nice footwear where you can just slip into some slides and then put on your cleats, it's something easy to walk around the facility and do all that with."

Even if they're big green Hulk feet.

--ESPN reporters Brady Henderson, John Keim, Marc Raimondi, Mike Reiss and Nick Wagoner contributed to this story.

text:
The Detroit Lions EDGE position opposite Aidan Hutchinson has been a source of consternation for years - mainly due to injuries. Will adding a healthy, young Derrick Moore solve the problem?

The following are medical recaps of the key EDGE players for the Lions heading into training camp, as taken from Lions 2026 Training Camp Medical Preview: EDGE.

(Age at start of season in parentheses.) Click on player name for full medical report if available.

Aidan Hutchinson (26)

Medical concern level: 0/10

This elite EDGE had a fully healthy last season after his tib/fib fracture from the year prior. While he probably still has surgical hardware in that leg, there are no residual concerns.

OUTLOOK: Hutch has been excellent and may be ready to take his game to another level. Lowering his excessively high snap counts may actually help him get there.

Derrick Moore (23)

Medical concern level: 1/10

There was a pre-draft hamstring concern that raised my eyebrows, but fortunately no indications of any significant issues during OTA and minicamp. If it was truly just a minor hamstring, that’s not a concern.

In college at Michigan, Moore was healthy and reliable.

OUTLOOK: This rookie is being counted on to be a long-term complement to Hutchinson. If he can hit the ground running, the entire defense (especially the beleaguered secondary) will show a massive improvement.

DJ Wonnum (28)

Medical concern level: 3/10

Quad tendon and ankle surgeries in his past could have some residuals. He played 17 of 18 games last season which is a great sign. The remarkable history of MRSA and DVT should not be an issue.

OUTLOOK: Wonnum has some proven production with 30 sacks in his six-year career. The hope is that he can have a breakthrough season in his late 20’s.

title: Badgers hire former Ohio State, NFL LB to key front office role - Bucky's 5th Quarter

The Wisconsin Badgers have continued to add to their football front office staff, as they hired former Ohio State linebacker Curtis Grant Jr. as their Director of Player Development, he announced on Friday.
Grant has a connection to head coach Luke Fickell, who was on the Ohio State staff from 2011-14.
Grant now joins Wisconsin’s staff in a key role, as the Badgers finalize their front office.
But in the front office, Wisconsin hired general manager Morocco Brown, who has an extensive NFL background.
They also brought in Bradie Ewing to be the Director of Player Engagement, while Darius Hicks was hired to be the next Director of Player Personnel.
text:
The Wisconsin Badgers have continued to add to their football front office staff, as they hired former Ohio State linebacker Curtis Grant Jr. as their Director of Player Development, he announced on Friday.

Grant, 33, was a five-star recruit coming out of high school, committing to Ohio State, where he played in 45 games and was a member of the team’s 2014 National Championship team. He went on to be an undrafted free agent in the 2015 NFL Draft.

Grant spent three years in the NFL, moving around several practice squads before playing 10 games with the New York Giants in 2017. However, a knee injury ended his season, and he didn’t play in the NFL again.

Grant has a connection to head coach Luke Fickell, who was on the Ohio State staff from 2011-14. Grant now joins Wisconsin’s staff in a key role, as the Badgers finalize their front office.

Wisconsin has made quite a few moves with its staff this offseason. Chris Worley, who was the previous Director of Player Development, was moved to an on-field role, coaching the nickel corners as an assistant defensive back.

But in the front office, Wisconsin hired general manager Morocco Brown, who has an extensive NFL background. They also brought in Bradie Ewing to be the Director of Player Engagement, while Darius Hicks was hired to be the next Director of Player Personnel.

Now, Curtis Grant becomes the latest hire for the Badgers.

title: Why can't MetLife Stadium have grass for NFL games? | Big Blue View
description:
It had to be galling to New York Giants (and Jets) fans when MetLife Stadium was announced as one of the venues for the 2026 World Cup.

The grass grown by a local sod farm in British Columbia for Vancouver BC Place World Cup matches received rave reviews from players.

text:
It had to be galling to New York Giants (and Jets) fans when MetLife Stadium was announced as one of the venues for the 2026 World Cup. Not because fans are protective of their beautiful stadium (which MetLife most certainly is not), but because soccer’s governing body FIFA requires that all matches be played on a grass pitch rather than artificial turf.

Giants fans have been pleading for years for the Mara and Tisch families to replace the infamous turf at MetLife, author of Malik Nabers’ season-ending ACL injury in Game 4 of the 2025 season, with real grass, as so many other NFL stadiums have. It’s fallen on deaf ears…until this year. Money talks, and for several more days, we will see MetLife in all its natural grass glory until the final match between Spain and Argentina is over.

FIFA worries about ACL injuries too, because they are fairly common in soccer. One recent study found that there were 1.7 ACL injuries per 10,000 athlete events. This has led to the “FIFA 11+” injury prevention program. NFL football is different from soccer in the movements and stresses it places on the human body, and unlike the sport-wide FIFA 11+ protocol, injury prevention in the NFL is overseen by individual teams rather than there being a league-wide protocol. A recent study concluded that over a four-year period there were 149 ligament tears in 1213 games played, with the rate being slightly higher on turf (0.132 tears per game) than grass (0.111 tears per game), a statistically insignificant difference. During the World Cup there has been one ACL tear, to Belgium’s Amadou Onana in Belgium’s victory over the US in Seattle. That’s one injury in 102 matches, much lower (0.0098) than the NFL rate. But, small number statistics and different sports.

That said, we now have data on whether two NFL teams sharing the same field can support real grass thanks to FIFA’s experiment. I don’t know if the NFL does this for grass fields, but FIFA requires that sod be grown with a plastic layer underneath, which forces roots to spread horizontally and create a dense grass layer. The grass grown by a local sod farm in British Columbia for Vancouver BC Place World Cup matches received rave reviews from players.

Alas, the same could not be said for the grass grown for MetLife World Cup matches. After the first two matches, The Athletic reported that:

With two matches played there, and six more to come including the final, the condition of the playing surface is already raising concerns. High-profile players such as Brazil star Vinicius Junior and France’s Adrien Rabiot described the pitch as dry and difficult to play on, while Rabiot’s coach Didier Deschamps said it was “special”. (He didn’t mean it in a good way.)

Vinicious Junior said that:

“Because of the weather and the heat, the grass dries out quickly and the game ends up being very slow. We can’t build up a rhythm,” the Real Madrid player told TNT Sports Brazil.

“That makes things difficult because we want to play. We want to move the ball from one side to the other and this disrupts our game. But we have to adapt because I believe it will be like this all tournament.

France head coach Didier Deschamps and player Adrien Rabiot called the grass at MetLife Stadium “a special surface — it’s different.”

“We need to get used to this. There might be some cement below the grass. You have very short shards of grass here. But we do adjust. This does create a change, but we take these technicalities into account.”

Rabiot shared a similar assessment. “Well,” he started, “the pitch was… I don’t know if I’d even call it that. It seemed more like an artificial pitch. It was hard and rigid, but it’s like that for every team. You need to adapt to the conditions.

“I hope we find better pitches in our other games.”

It didn’t pass the eye test either:

The criticism goes back even to last year when Club World Cup matches were held at MetLife. NFL players overwhelmingly advocate for grass fields, not just because of the injury issue but also due to what they see as increased wear and tear on their bodies overall after games on turf relative to grass:

But what is it with MetLife specifically? If BC Place and others can do it, why not here? There are a couple of reasons. One is just the luck of the draw as far as weather goes. There are cool season and warm season grasses. For a tournament played in June and July in New Jersey, of course you’d plant a warm season (Bermuda) grass. Just one problem - Mother Nature didn’t get the memo. May was not as consistently warm as expected, and the Bermuda grass didn’t grow fast enough. Unlike BC Place, which used sod from a local grower, MetLife had to have sod trucked in on a 12-hour drive from North Carolina because the planned usage of a local New Jersey supplier was prevented by the Northeast’s harsh winter.

That said, MetLife will end up hosting eight World Cup matches matches in a month and a half, more than it will host for the Giants and Jets combined over a similar time period.

There’s another factor that is specific to MetLife, though, and this may be the death knell for the hopes of a permanent grass field. Here is the Met Life schedule starting August 1:

Aug. 1-2: BTS (Korean boy band, in case like me you had to look them up)

Aug 7-6: Chris Brown and Usher

Aug. 12: Guns N’ Roses

Aug. 14: Jets - Tampa Bay preseason game

Aug, 15: Giants - Vikings preseason game

Aug, 21, 22, 25, 26: Bruno Mars

Aug. 28: Jets - Giants preseason game

Sept. 4-5: Ed Sheeran

Sept. 11: BigBang (another Korean boy band)

Sept. 13: Giants - Cowboys season opener

Sept. 17-18: Karol G (Colombian singer, had to look her up, too)

Sept. 20: Jets - Packers

Sept. 25: AC/DC

Sept. 25: Giants - Titans

You get the idea. For the next two months, MetLife is going to be packed with events, presumably with tons of people on the field. This, in addition to the cost, may be the real reason that the Giants and Jets are so resistant to going to grass. And regarding that latter point, remember that moving to grass permanently is something that Jets owner Woody Johnson would have to agree to and split the cost for, not just the Maras and Tisches.

Perhaps the World Cup was a turning point, though. Maybe some day the owners will finally listen to the players on this issue, and we’ll hear the players shout in unison: “Go-o-o-o-o-o-al!”

In the short term, though, don’t expect anything but a yellow card.
